subject: estimation issues with multistate m-array in jags

messages.author: 0c6a7a3cad7e0b17
messages.subject: estimation issues with multistate m-array in jags
parts:
Hello,

I am having some trouble with a joint analysis of live recapture and dead recovery data using a multi-state m-array format in JAGs. I am running simulations based on an “ideal” data set that includes CMR and recoveries every year – and in this case the code works without a problem and the posteriors include truth. Therefore, I know this code is working. However, I am trying to fit the model based on data similar to data scenario which includes 3 years of CMR+recoveries followed by 9 years with recoveries only followed by 2 years of CMR+recoveries (i.e., dead recoveries are recorded in every year of the study but capture-mark-recapture surveys only occur in the first 3 years and the last 2 years of the study). I can fit these data in JAGs using the state-space format and the estimates are fine. But when I try to fit these data in JAGs using the m-array format the estimates are biased (high or low depends on the parameter). This leads me to believe there is something about the code within JAGs that is causing this issue, but I am not certain.

 

Has anyone else run into this problem before? I have included my code and would appreciate any help you can provide!

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Multi-state joint live-dead m-array model

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

n.occasions <- 14

n.states <- 3

n.obs <- 3


S <- 0.9

p <- matrix(0.3,1,n.occasions-1)

p[3] <- p[4] <- p[5] <- p[6] <- p[7] <- p[8] <- p[9]<- p[10] <- p[11]  <- 0 # no recaptures in these years

r <- 0.2

marked <- matrix(0, ncol = n.states, nrow = n.occasions)

for(t in 1:n.occasions){

  marked[t,1] <- 100

}

marked[4:12,1] <- 0 # no individuals released or recaptured in these years


totrel <- sum(marked) * (n.occasions-1)


PSI.STATE <- array(NA, dim=c(n.states,n.states,totrel,n.occasions-1))

for (i in 1:totrel){

  for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

    PSI.STATE[,,i,t] <- matrix(c(

      S, 1-S, 0,

      0, 0, 1,

      0, 0, 1

    ), nrow=n.states, byrow=T)

  } #t

} #i

PSI.OBS <- array(NA, dim=c(n.states,n.obs,totrel,n.occasions-1))

for (i in 1:totrel){

  for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

    PSI.OBS[,,i,t] <- matrix(c(

      p[t], 0, 1-p[t],

      0, r, 1-r,

      0, 0, 1

    ), nrow=n.states, byrow=T)

  } #t

} #i


# Define function to simulate multistate capture-recapture data

simul.ms <- function(PSI.STATE, PSI.OBS, marked, unobservable = NA){

  # Unobservable: number of state that is unobservable

  n.occasions <- dim(PSI.STATE)[4] + 1

  CH <- CH.TRUE <- matrix(NA, ncol = n.occasions, nrow = sum(marked))

  # Define a vector with the occasion of marking

  mark.occ <- matrix(0, ncol = dim(PSI.STATE)[1], nrow = sum(marked))

  g <- colSums(marked)

  for (s in 1:dim(PSI.STATE)[1]){

    if (g[s]==0) next  # To avoid error message if nothing to replace

    mark.occ[(cumsum(g[1:s])-g[s]+1)[s]:cumsum(g[1:s])[s],s] <-

      rep(1:n.occasions, marked[1:n.occasions,s])

  } #s

  for (i in 1:sum(marked)){

    for (s in 1:dim(PSI.STATE)[1]){

      if (mark.occ[i,s]==0) next

      first <- mark.occ[i,s]

      CH[i,first] <- s

      CH.TRUE[i,first] <- s

    } #s

    for (t in (first+1):n.occasions){

      # Multinomial trials for state transitions

      if (first==n.occasions) next

      state <- which(rmultinom(1, 1, PSI.STATE[CH.TRUE[i,t-1],,i,t-1])==1)

      CH.TRUE[i,t] <- state

      # Multinomial trials for observation process

      event <- which(rmultinom(1, 1, PSI.OBS[CH.TRUE[i,t],,i,t-1])==1)

      CH[i,t] <- event

    } #t

  } #i

  # Replace the NA and the highest state number (dead) in the file by 0

  CH[is.na(CH)] <- 0

  CH[CH==dim(PSI.STATE)[1]] <- 0

  CH[CH==unobservable] <- 0

  id <- numeric(0)

  for (i in 1:dim(CH)[1]){

    z <- min(which(CH[i,]!=0))

    ifelse(z==dim(CH)[2], id <- c(id,i), id <- c(id))

  }

  return(list(CH=CH[-id,], CH.TRUE=CH.TRUE[-id,]))

  # CH: capture histories to be used

  # CH.TRUE: capture histories with perfect observation

}

# Execute function

sim <- simul.ms(PSI.STATE, PSI.OBS, marked)

CH <- sim$CH


# Define function to create a multistate m-array from capture history data

marray <- function(ch, unobs = 0){

  ns <- length(table(ch)) - 1 + unobs

  no <- ncol(ch)

  out <- matrix(0, ncol = ns*(no-1)+1, nrow = ns*(no-1))

  # Remove capture histories of individuals that are marked at last occasion

  get.first <- function(x) min(which(x!=0))

  first <- apply(ch, 1, get.first)

  last.only <- which(first==no)

  if (length(last.only) > 0) ch <- ch[-last.only,]

  # Compute m-array

  for (i in 1:nrow(ch)){

    cap.occ <- which(ch[i,]!=0)

    state <- ch[i,cap.occ]

    if (length(state) == 1) {

      out[state[1]+ns*(cap.occ[1]-1), ns*(no-1)+1] <- out[state[1]+

                                                            ns*(cap.occ[1]-1), ns*(no-1)+1] + 1

    }

    if (length(state) > 1) {

      for (t in 2:length(cap.occ)){

        out[(cap.occ[t-1]-1)*ns+state[t-1], (cap.occ[t]-2)*

              ns+state[t]] <- out[(cap.occ[t-1]-1)*ns+state[t-1], (cap.occ[t]-2)*

                                    ns+state[t]] + 1

      } # t

      if (max(cap.occ) < no){

        out[(cap.occ[t]-1)*ns+state[t], ns*(no-1)+1] <- out[(cap.occ[t]-1)*

                                                              ns+state[t], ns*(no-1)+1] + 1

      } # i

    } # if

  } # i

  return(out)

}    

# Excecute function to create m-array from capture history data

marr <- marray(CH)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

# Analysis in JAGS

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

sink("marray.jags")

cat("

model {


for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

    S[t] <- muS

    r[t] <- mur

}

p[1] <- mup

p[2] <- mup

for (t in 3:11){

  p[t] <- 0

}

p[12] <- mup

p[13] <- mup


muS ~ dunif(0.0001, 0.999)

mur ~ dunif(0.0001, 0.999)

mup ~ dunif(0.0001, 0.999)


# Define state-transition and observation matrices: 

# Define probabilities of state S(t+1) given S(t)

for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

  psm[1,t,1] <- S[t]     # Survive and remain alive

  psm[1,t,2] <- 1 - S[t] # Alive to recently dead transition


  psm[2,t,1] <- 0

  psm[2,t,2] <- 0

}


# Define probabilities of observation at t given state at (t)

for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

  pom[1,t] <- p[t]

  pom[2,t] <- r[t]

  

  # Calculate probability of non-observation (dqm) and reshape the        

  # array for the observation probabilities   

  for (s in 1:mns){

    dpm[s,t,s] <- pom[s,t]

    dqm[s,t,s] <- 1-pom[s,t]

  } # s

  for (s in 1:(mns-1)){

    for (m in (s+1):mns){

      dpm[s,t,m] <- 0

      dqm[s,t,m] <- 0

    } # m

  } # s

  for (s in 2:mns){

    for (m in 1:(s-1)){

      dpm[s,t,m] <- 0

      dqm[s,t,m] <- 0

    } # m

  } # s

} # t


# Define the multinomial likelihood for all released 

for (t in 1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)){

  marr[t,1:(n.occasions*mns-(mns-1))] ~ dmulti(prm[t,], relm[t])

}


# Define cell probabilities of the multistate m-array   

# Define matrix U: product of probabilities of state-transition and 

# non-encounter 

for (t in 1:(n.occasions-2)){

  Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- onesm

  for (j in (t+1):(n.occasions-1)){

    Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),

    (j-2)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,t,] %*% dqm[,t,]

  } #j

} #t

Um[(n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns), (n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns)] <- onesm


# Diagonal

for (t in 1:(n.occasions-2)){

  prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <-   

   Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,t,] %*% dpm[,t,]

  # Above main diagonal

  for (j in (t+1):(n.occasions-1)){

    prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), 

     (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,j,] %*% dpm[,j,]

  } #j

} #t


# Last Diagonal

prm[(n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns), (n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns)] <-  

 psm[,n.occasions-1,] %*% dpm[,n.occasions-1,]

# Below main diagonal

for (t in 2:(n.occasions-1)){

  for (j in 1:(t-1)){

    prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- zerom

  } #j

} #t


# Last column: probability of non-recapture

for (t in 1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)){

  prm[t,(n.occasions*mns-(mns-1))] <- 1-sum(prm[t,1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)])

} #t


}

",fill = TRUE)

sink()


mns <- 2

jags.data <- list(marr = marr, 

                  n.occasions = 14, relm = rowSums(marr),

                  mns = mns, zerom = matrix(0, ncol = mns, nrow = mns),

                  onesm = diag(mns))

inits <- function(){list(muS = runif(1,0.0001,0.999), mur = runif(1,0.0001,0.999),

                         mup = runif(1,0.0001,0.999))}

parameters <- c("muS","mur","mup", "S", "p", "r")


ni <- 15000; nt <- 5; na <- 10000; nb <- 5000; nc <- 3

set.seed(runif(1,1,999)) 

ms_sim <- jags(jags.data, inits=inits, parameters, "marray.jags", 

               n.chains = nc, n.iter = ni, n.burnin = nb, 

               n.adapt = na, n.thin = nt, parallel = F)

print(ms_sim, digits = 3)

parts:
Hi Kylee,

When you formulate a multistate model that jointly analyses live recaptures and dead recoveries, you need to include 2 death states (recently dead and long-time dead). The latter is absorbing and non-observable. It is needed, because otherwise a dead individual can be repeatedly be recovered. See Chapter 9.5 in the BPA book.

Best wishes

Michael

parameters <- c("muS","mur","mup", "S", "p", "r")


ni <- 15000; nt <- 5; na <- 10000; nb <- 5000; nc <- 3

set.seed(runif(1,1,999)) 

ms_sim <- jags(jags.data, inits=inits, parameters, "marray.jags", 

               n.chains = nc, n.iter = ni, n.burnin = nb, 

               n.adapt = na, n.thin = nt, parallel = F)

parts:
Hi Michael, thank you for your quick response. I have run this model with and without the 'dead absorbing' state in the m-array format and the results are the same. I tested that again this morning by running the model with and without the dead absorbing state with CMRR data for all years and there were no estimation issues in either example. However, when there are only recoveries for a period of time between CMR surveys the estimation issue (bias in recovery probability + survival) remains regardless of the additional dead state. This issue does not occur when running the same data through the state-space format. 

I am wondering if anyone else has experience running CMRR models when there are some years with CMR and years with recoveries only but analyzed in the m-array format. Or, if anyone knows whether the m-array code needs to be adapted within jags to deal with such a scenario. I have two projects that would greatly benefit from the time saved using the m-array over the state-space format so I would love to figure this out! Thank you!

On Tuesday, September 1, 2020 at 12:31:33 AM UTC-6 Schaub Michael wrote:
Hi Kylee,

When you formulate a multistate model that jointly analyses live recaptures and dead recoveries, you need to include 2 death states (recently dead and long-time dead). The latter is absorbing and non-observable. It is needed, because otherwise a dead individual can be repeatedly be recovered. See Chapter 9.5 in the BPA book.

Best wishes

Michael

Von: hmec...@googlegroups.com [hmec...@googlegroups.com]" im Auftrag von "Kylee Dunham [kdu...@ualberta.ca]
Gesendet: Freitag, 28. August 2020 00:07
An: hmecology: Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology
Betreff: estimation issues with multistate m-array in jags

Hello,

I am having some trouble with a joint analysis of live recapture and dead recovery data using a multi-state m-array format in JAGs. I am running simulations based on an “ideal” data set that includes CMR and recoveries every year – and in this case the code works without a problem and the posteriors include truth. Therefore, I know this code is working. However, I am trying to fit the model based on data similar to data scenario which includes 3 years of CMR+recoveries followed by 9 years with recoveries only followed by 2 years of CMR+recoveries (i.e., dead recoveries are recorded in every year of the study but capture-mark-recapture surveys only occur in the first 3 years and the last 2 years of the study). I can fit these data in JAGs using the state-space format and the estimates are fine. But when I try to fit these data in JAGs using the m-array format the estimates are biased (high or low depends on the parameter). This leads me to believe there is something about the code within JAGs that is causing this issue, but I am not certain.

 

Has anyone else run into this problem before? I have included my code and would appreciate any help you can provide!

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Multi-state joint live-dead m-array model

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

n.occasions <- 14

n.states <- 3

n.obs <- 3


S <- 0.9

p <- matrix(0.3,1,n.occasions-1)

p[3] <- p[4] <- p[5] <- p[6] <- p[7] <- p[8] <- p[9]<- p[10] <- p[11]  <- 0 # no recaptures in these years

r <- 0.2

marked <- matrix(0, ncol = n.states, nrow = n.occasions)

for(t in 1:n.occasions){

  marked[t,1] <- 100

}

marked[4:12,1] <- 0 # no individuals released or recaptured in these years


totrel <- sum(marked) * (n.occasions-1)


PSI.STATE <- array(NA, dim=c(n.states,n.states,totrel,n.occasions-1))

for (i in 1:totrel){

  for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

    PSI.STATE[,,i,t] <- matrix(c(

      S, 1-S, 0,

      0, 0, 1,

      0, 0, 1

    ), nrow=n.states, byrow=T)

  } #t

} #i

PSI.OBS <- array(NA, dim=c(n.states,n.obs,totrel,n.occasions-1))

for (i in 1:totrel){

  for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

    PSI.OBS[,,i,t] <- matrix(c(

      p[t], 0, 1-p[t],

      0, r, 1-r,

      0, 0, 1

    ), nrow=n.states, byrow=T)

  } #t

} #i


# Define function to simulate multistate capture-recapture data

simul.ms <- function(PSI.STATE, PSI.OBS, marked, unobservable = NA){

  # Unobservable: number of state that is unobservable

  n.occasions <- dim(PSI.STATE)[4] + 1

  CH <- CH.TRUE <- matrix(NA, ncol = n.occasions, nrow = sum(marked))

  # Define a vector with the occasion of marking

  mark.occ <- matrix(0, ncol = dim(PSI.STATE)[1], nrow = sum(marked))

  g <- colSums(marked)

  for (s in 1:dim(PSI.STATE)[1]){

    if (g[s]==0) next  # To avoid error message if nothing to replace

    mark.occ[(cumsum(g[1:s])-g[s]+1)[s]:cumsum(g[1:s])[s],s] <-

      rep(1:n.occasions, marked[1:n.occasions,s])

  } #s

  for (i in 1:sum(marked)){

    for (s in 1:dim(PSI.STATE)[1]){

      if (mark.occ[i,s]==0) next

      first <- mark.occ[i,s]

      CH[i,first] <- s

      CH.TRUE[i,first] <- s

    } #s

    for (t in (first+1):n.occasions){

      # Multinomial trials for state transitions

      if (first==n.occasions) next

      state <- which(rmultinom(1, 1, PSI.STATE[CH.TRUE[i,t-1],,i,t-1])==1)

      CH.TRUE[i,t] <- state

      # Multinomial trials for observation process

      event <- which(rmultinom(1, 1, PSI.OBS[CH.TRUE[i,t],,i,t-1])==1)

      CH[i,t] <- event

    } #t

  } #i

  # Replace the NA and the highest state number (dead) in the file by 0

  CH[is.na(CH)] <- 0

  CH[CH==dim(PSI.STATE)[1]] <- 0

  CH[CH==unobservable] <- 0

  id <- numeric(0)

  for (i in 1:dim(CH)[1]){

    z <- min(which(CH[i,]!=0))

    ifelse(z==dim(CH)[2], id <- c(id,i), id <- c(id))

  }

  return(list(CH=CH[-id,], CH.TRUE=CH.TRUE[-id,]))

  # CH: capture histories to be used

  # CH.TRUE: capture histories with perfect observation

}

# Execute function

sim <- simul.ms(PSI.STATE, PSI.OBS, marked)

CH <- sim$CH


# Define function to create a multistate m-array from capture history data

marray <- function(ch, unobs = 0){

  ns <- length(table(ch)) - 1 + unobs

  no <- ncol(ch)

  out <- matrix(0, ncol = ns*(no-1)+1, nrow = ns*(no-1))

  # Remove capture histories of individuals that are marked at last occasion

  get.first <- function(x) min(which(x!=0))

  first <- apply(ch, 1, get.first)

  last.only <- which(first==no)

  if (length(last.only) > 0) ch <- ch[-last.only,]

  # Compute m-array

  for (i in 1:nrow(ch)){

    cap.occ <- which(ch[i,]!=0)

    state <- ch[i,cap.occ]

    if (length(state) == 1) {

      out[state[1]+ns*(cap.occ[1]-1), ns*(no-1)+1] <- out[state[1]+

                                                            ns*(cap.occ[1]-1), ns*(no-1)+1] + 1

    }

    if (length(state) > 1) {

      for (t in 2:length(cap.occ)){

        out[(cap.occ[t-1]-1)*ns+state[t-1], (cap.occ[t]-2)*

              ns+state[t]] <- out[(cap.occ[t-1]-1)*ns+state[t-1], (cap.occ[t]-2)*

                                    ns+state[t]] + 1

      } # t

      if (max(cap.occ) < no){

        out[(cap.occ[t]-1)*ns+state[t], ns*(no-1)+1] <- out[(cap.occ[t]-1)*

                                                              ns+state[t], ns*(no-1)+1] + 1

      } # i

    } # if

  } # i

  return(out)

}    

# Excecute function to create m-array from capture history data

marr <- marray(CH)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

# Analysis in JAGS

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

sink("marray.jags")

cat("

model {


for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

    S[t] <- muS

    r[t] <- mur

}

p[1] <- mup

p[2] <- mup

for (t in 3:11){

  p[t] <- 0

}

p[12] <- mup

p[13] <- mup


muS ~ dunif(0.0001, 0.999)

mur ~ dunif(0.0001, 0.999)

mup ~ dunif(0.0001, 0.999)


# Define state-transition and observation matrices: 

# Define probabilities of state S(t+1) given S(t)

for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

  psm[1,t,1] <- S[t]     # Survive and remain alive

  psm[1,t,2] <- 1 - S[t] # Alive to recently dead transition


  psm[2,t,1] <- 0

  psm[2,t,2] <- 0

}


# Define probabilities of observation at t given state at (t)

for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

  pom[1,t] <- p[t]

  pom[2,t] <- r[t]

  

  # Calculate probability of non-observation (dqm) and reshape the        

  # array for the observation probabilities   

  for (s in 1:mns){

    dpm[s,t,s] <- pom[s,t]

    dqm[s,t,s] <- 1-pom[s,t]

  } # s

  for (s in 1:(mns-1)){

    for (m in (s+1):mns){

      dpm[s,t,m] <- 0

      dqm[s,t,m] <- 0

    } # m

  } # s

  for (s in 2:mns){

    for (m in 1:(s-1)){

      dpm[s,t,m] <- 0

      dqm[s,t,m] <- 0

    } # m

  } # s

} # t


# Define the multinomial likelihood for all released 

for (t in 1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)){

  marr[t,1:(n.occasions*mns-(mns-1))] ~ dmulti(prm[t,], relm[t])

}


# Define cell probabilities of the multistate m-array   

# Define matrix U: product of probabilities of state-transition and 

# non-encounter 

for (t in 1:(n.occasions-2)){

  Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- onesm

  for (j in (t+1):(n.occasions-1)){

    Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),

    (j-2)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,t,] %*% dqm[,t,]

  } #j

} #t

Um[(n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns), (n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns)] <- onesm


# Diagonal

for (t in 1:(n.occasions-2)){

  prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <-   

   Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,t,] %*% dpm[,t,]

  # Above main diagonal

  for (j in (t+1):(n.occasions-1)){

    prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), 

     (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,j,] %*% dpm[,j,]

  } #j

} #t


# Last Diagonal

prm[(n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns), (n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns)] <-  

 psm[,n.occasions-1,] %*% dpm[,n.occasions-1,]

# Below main diagonal

for (t in 2:(n.occasions-1)){

  for (j in 1:(t-1)){

    prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- zerom

  } #j

} #t


# Last column: probability of non-recapture

for (t in 1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)){

  prm[t,(n.occasions*mns-(mns-1))] <- 1-sum(prm[t,1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)])

} #t


}

",fill = TRUE)

sink()


mns <- 2

jags.data <- list(marr = marr, 

                  n.occasions = 14, relm = rowSums(marr),

                  mns = mns, zerom = matrix(0, ncol = mns, nrow = mns),

                  onesm = diag(mns))

inits <- function(){list(muS = runif(1,0.0001,0.999), mur = runif(1,0.0001,0.999),

                         mup = runif(1,0.0001,0.999))}

parameters <- c("muS","mur","mup", "S", "p", "r")


ni <- 15000; nt <- 5; na <- 10000; nb <- 5000; nc <- 3

set.seed(runif(1,1,999)) 

ms_sim <- jags(jags.data, inits=inits, parameters, "marray.jags", 

               n.chains = nc, n.iter = ni, n.burnin = nb, 

               n.adapt = na, n.thin = nt, parallel = F)

print(ms_sim, digits = 3)
